description: Replace the dense LLM text reports on the Reports page with three interactive Chart.js visualizations: income vs spending bar chart, spending-by-category doughnut, and category trends line chart. Keep Ask Pulse and What-If below the charts. Add a new multi-month trends API endpoint to power all three charts from a single request.

timing.gatingCondition: None. Budget snapshots and categories are already stable.

principles: Charts should communicate financial patterns at a glance, replacing paragraph-form LLM summaries
One API call should power all three charts to minimize database round-trips
Dark and light theme support must work automatically via CSS variables
Reuse existing Chart.js 4.x dependency and category color data from the database
Ask Pulse and What-If remain available as interactive tools below the visualizations

techStack.database: PostgreSQL budget_snapshots + transactions for aggregated trend data
techStack.testing: node:test for API and data-shaping coverage; manual chart rendering checks in browser until a DOM/browser harness is added

userStories.title: Multi-month trends API endpoint
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/budget/trends returns 6 months of data by default
Response includes per-month income, spending, net cash flow, and category breakdown
Current (in-progress) month uses a fresh snapshot for live data
months query param is capped at 12
Endpoint requires parent authentication
userStories.testStrategy: node:test integration coverage for response shape, month clamping, snapshot generation behavior, and parent auth guard.

userStories.title: Income vs Spending bar chart
acceptanceCriteria: Bar chart shows income (green) and spending (red) per month for 6 months
Net cash flow line overlays the bars
Month labels formatted as short names (Oct, Nov, etc.)
Tooltips show currency-formatted values
Works in both dark and light themes
userStories.testStrategy: Automate dataset-shaping helpers with node:test once extracted; until then use manual browser checks for canvas rendering, tooltips, and theme toggle.

userStories.title: Spending by category doughnut chart
acceptanceCriteria: Doughnut chart shows category breakdown for a selected month
Month selector dropdown defaults to current month
Uses category colors from the database
Changing month re-renders only the doughnut chart
Same destroy/recreate pattern as kids.js
userStories.testStrategy: node:test coverage for category grouping rules (top 8 plus Other) if extracted into helpers, plus manual browser verification for month switching and no-data recovery.

userStories.title: Category trends line chart
acceptanceCriteria: Line chart shows top 5 spending categories over 6 months
Each line uses the category's database color
Smooth curves with tension
Legend identifies each category
Readable in both themes
userStories.testStrategy: node:test coverage for top-5 category selection if extracted into helpers, plus manual browser verification for legend readability and theme contrast.

userStories.title: Reports page restructure
acceptanceCriteria: Monthly Reports and Weekly Digest accordion sections are removed
Three chart sections appear above Ask Pulse
Ask Pulse, What-If, and Query History remain functional
Charts are responsive on mobile
Loading state while charts fetch data
userStories.testStrategy: node:test integration coverage for retained Ask/What-If history APIs; manual verification on desktop/mobile viewport for layout, chart stacking, and interaction continuity.

medium: Budget snapshots may not exist for older months if backfill was never run — endpoint should handle sparse data gracefully
low: Chart.js CDN availability — already accepted risk from kids.html usage
Category colors may be null for some categories — fallback to accent color

preFlightChecklist: Verify budget_snapshots table has data for recent months
Confirm Chart.js CDN script loads correctly on reports.html
Check that category colors exist in the database for major categories

executionSlices.name: Slice A: Backend trends endpoint
notes: Query budget_snapshots + income from transactions in 2-3 SQL queries
Generate fresh snapshot for current month before querying

executionSlices.name: Slice B: Frontend charts
executionSlices.goal: Replace report sections with three Chart.js visualizations.
notes: Single API call powers all three charts

executionSlices.name: Slice C: Testing strategy
executionSlices.goal: Cover stable logic in node:test and document manual checks for browser-only behavior.
notes: Add endpoint integration tests for /api/budget/trends covering defaults, auth, month bounds, and live snapshot refresh behavior
Prefer extracting pure dataset-building helpers from public/reports.js and test those helpers with node:test rather than trying to unit test Chart.js rendering
Do not add Playwright or jsdom as part of this feature; this repo currently uses zero test dependencies
Document a short manual checklist for canvas rendering, month switching, no-data recovery, theme toggle, and mobile layout

automatedNow: GET /api/budget/trends returns expected periods and monthly objects for seeded data
months query parameter clamps to the supported range (1-12)
months=1 minimum bound returns exactly 1 period
Non-numeric months param (e.g. abc) falls back to default 6
Periods are chronological (oldest first) with current month last
Spending total equals sum of category spent values per month
net_cash_flow equals income minus spending per month
Category entries include id, name, spent, color, icon fields
Missing prior snapshots are generated on demand before trend data is returned
Current month snapshot is refreshed so current-period data stays live
Ask Pulse and What-If backend history remains covered by existing API tests
recommendedNext: Extract pure helper functions from public/reports.js for income/spending datasets, doughnut category grouping, and top-category trend selection
Add node:test unit coverage for those helpers, including empty months and top-8/top-5 truncation rules
If the team later wants DOM automation, add a lightweight DOM harness only after multiple pages need it
manualChecklist: Load reports.html as a parent and confirm all three chart canvases render
Switch the doughnut month selector to a populated month and a no-data month, then back again
Toggle light and dark theme and confirm axis labels, legends, and grid lines remain readable after the toggle without reload
Submit an Ask Pulse prompt and a What-If scenario and confirm the history list refreshes immediately
Check a narrow mobile viewport to confirm cards stack cleanly and charts remain visible without horizontal overflow
nonGoals: Pixel-perfect screenshot testing of Chart.js output
Adding Playwright or another browser test framework solely for this feature
